problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{22}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A$ $=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]$ if its determinant is $-16.$
worked_solution:
Since we want the entry ${a}_{22}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{22}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{22} & =(-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =4-0 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{22}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{22}=\frac{1}{-16}\cdot 4=-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
